skill.name: create-subagent
skill.description: Guidance for creating Claude Code subagents, configuring tool scopes, and using Task delegation patterns safely.
skill.summary: Create reusable Claude Code subagents with templates, tool scopes, and delegation patterns.
skill.author: Cygnusfear

security_audit.summary: Most static command and network-recon findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, inline code, or agent template prose. The confirmed risk is persistent user-level agent configuration through ~/.claude/agents. Additional context shows unsafe permission guidance for bypassing prompts and inheriting all tools.

remediation.issue: User-level hidden agent files persist across projects.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer project-level .claude/agents examples, require explicit user consent before writing ~/.claude/agents, and document the persistence risk.

remediation.issue: Permission guidance includes bypassPermissions and full tool inheritance.
remediation.suggestion: Add clear warnings, default examples to least-privilege tools, and require explicit user request before using bypassPermissions or inherited full tools.

remediation.issue: Command examples may be mistaken for automatic execution.
remediation.suggestion: Label CLI snippets as manual examples and state that the skill should not run setup commands without confirmation.

static_findings.snippet: - ALWAYS write tests that fail first, then pass
- ALWAYS assume attackers have source code access
| `general-purpose` | Configurable | All | Complex research, multi-step operations |
| `plan` | Sonnet | Read, Glob, Grep, Bash | Codebase research before planning |
| `name` | Unique identifier (lowercase letters, numbers, hyphens only, max 64 chars) |
| `description` | When the agent should be used (include "PROACTIVELY" for auto-invocation) |
| `tools` | Comma-separated list | Specific tools to allow. Omit to inherit all. |
| `model` | `sonnet`, `opus`, `haiku`, `inherit` | Model to use. Default: inherit from session. |
| `permissionMode` | See below | How permissions are handled |
| `skills` | Comma-separated list | Skills to auto-load when agent starts |
2. **Read-only for analysis**: Use `Read, Glob, Grep` for review agents

content.value_statement: Teams often need specialized AI assistants, but subagent setup can be inconsistent and over-permissive. This skill provides templates, configuration guidance, and delegation patterns for reusable Claude Code subagents.
actual_capabilities: Explains project-level and user-level locations for Claude Code agent files.
Shows file-based subagent definitions with frontmatter fields for tools, models, permissions, and skills.
Describes Task tool invocation for dynamic, parallel, and resumed subagent work.
Provides templates for review, debugging, research, testing, documentation, security, and refactoring agents.
Lists troubleshooting steps for agent invocation, tool selection, and behavior correction.
Recommends least-privilege tool selection for analysis and review agents.
limitations: It does not create or validate agent files automatically.
Examples include powerful tools and permission modes that require careful review.
Guidance is specific to Claude Code subagents and may not fit other agent platforms.
It does not prove that a generated agent will behave safely after installation.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Review Agents
use_cases.description: Create shared project agents for code review, debugging, and test writing with consistent prompts and tool scopes.

use_cases.title: Design Safer Agent Permissions
use_cases.description: Compare read-only, edit-capable, and full-access agent patterns before approving subagent definitions.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Parallel Research
use_cases.description: Use Task dispatch patterns to split independent codebase research and synthesize the results.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Reviewer
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for one project-level agent
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a project-level Claude Code subagent for code review. Use read-only tools, clear trigger conditions, and a concise output format.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Debugging Agent
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate setup for recurring failure analysis
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a debugging subagent for this repository. Include its role, workflow, allowed tools, failure handling, and verification expectations.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Least-Privilege Agent Set
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning for several specialized agents
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan three Claude Code subagents for review, testing, and documentation. Justify each tool choice and avoid broad permissions unless required.

prompt_templates.title: Orchestrate Parallel Research
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced delegation across independent work streams
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a parallel Task workflow for researching authentication, authorization, and session handling. Include a final synthesis agent and success criteria.

output_examples.input: Create a code review subagent for a backend service.
output_examples.output: A focused reviewer definition with read-only tools, security and maintainability checks, and prioritized findings format.

output_examples.input: Plan subagents for a large refactor.
output_examples.output: A proposed agent set with research, refactoring, testing, and synthesis responsibilities separated by tool scope.

output_examples.input: Troubleshoot why an agent is not invoked automatically.
output_examples.output: A short checklist covering description triggers, file location, naming conflicts, and frontmatter syntax.

best_practices: Use project-level agents when the behavior should stay tied to one repository.
Grant only the tools needed for the agent task and prefer read-only access for analysis.
Test each agent with representative tasks before relying on automatic invocation.
anti_patterns: Giving every agent full tool access by default.
Using user-level agents when project-level scope is enough.
Writing vague descriptions that make automatic invocation unpredictable.

faq.question: What does this skill help create?
faq.answer: It helps create Claude Code subagents with clear roles, tool permissions, workflows, and invocation rules.

faq.question: Does it support Task tool delegation?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains dynamic Task dispatch, parallel agent patterns, resumed agents, and synthesis workflows.

faq.question: Can it create persistent agent files?
faq.answer: It explains the required file locations and format, but the assistant or user must still create the files.

faq.question: Which tools should new agents receive?
faq.answer: Use the smallest tool set that can complete the task. Read-only tools are best for review and research.

faq.question: Is global user-level installation recommended?
faq.answer: Use global agents only when the same behavior is needed across projects and the user explicitly approves it.

faq.question: Does this skill work outside Claude Code?
faq.answer: The concepts may transfer, but the file format and Task examples are written for Claude Code.
